title: SpaceX stock closes below its IPO price for the first time since it went public
summary: Shares of SpaceX continued their sharp descent Thursday and closed below the company’s IPO price for the first time since its June public offering.
story: Shares of SpaceX continued their sharp descent Thursday and closed below the company’s IPO price for the first time since its June public offering.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.
The rocket maker’s shares slid more than 3% to close at $131.11. On June 11, the company had priced its record-setting IPO at $135 per share.

Later on Thursday, SpaceX shares fell as low at $124 per share in after-hours trading, after the company delayed the launch of its flagship Starship rocket. This was to be the company’s first space launch since it went public.
Designed to be reusable, the rocket is a cornerstone of SpaceX founder Elon Musk’s plans to expand satellite-based communications, send humans into space and, in theory, put AI data centers in orbit.
The company, whose businesses include Starlink satellite internet, the X social network and the artificial intelligence firm xAI, began trading on the Nasdaq exchange June 12.
While the company had a strong debut, with shares soaring 19% on their first day of trading to as high as $193, it’s largely been on a downward trajectory since then.
Even after being added to the prestigious Nasdaq 100 and Russell 1000 stock indexes, which ordinarily would have sparked buying, the stock has fallen every single day, except for one, since then.
Making matters worse for the stock, just days after raising $75 billion in its IPO, SpaceX issued $25 billion worth of additional debt.
Short sellers have also piled onto the company, and their paper bets are now reportedly approaching $4 billion.
Investors, many of whom were regular retail investors, who bought SpaceX shares at its Day 1 opening price of $150 have seen that investment contract by more than 11%.
SpaceX’s market value has also shrunk by more than $1.2 trillion from its peak, which it hit June 16. From its debut price of $150, the company’s value has contracted by almost $250 billion.

Musk, whose fortune now rests primarily in his SpaceX stake, saw his net worth surge from about $700 billion to as much as $1.32 trillion after the IPO. However, that has contracted along with shares, to about $850 billion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.
Musk has been unflinching in his confidence about the company. Shortly after the IPO, he wrote on social media that “SpaceX might be able to reach approximately $1T revenue in 2030.”
Despite a rocky few weeks of trading, Wall Street analysts are largely bullish on the company’s future.

But the pain for SpaceX shares could be just getting started. In the weeks ahead, SpaceX will likely issue its first earnings report as a public company. That event will trigger the first wave of stock-sale lockups expiring. This means some longtime shareholders would be allowed to begin selling their shares and cashing in on what were, for years, merely paper gains.

It’s not entirely unusual for a major IPO to perform poorly in the short term, however. When Facebook, now called Meta Platforms, debuted in 2012, its shares traded below its IPO price for more than a year. Uber also traded below its IPO price for months after its 2019 offering.
But these dips reversed themselves over time. As of Thursday, Meta shares were up more than 1,600% since its IPO, while Uber has posted a nearly 80% gain since its debut.

title: Kris Jenner Announces Death of Mother Mary Jo ‘MJ’ Shannon at 91. Read the Emotional Statement
summary: Mary Jo “MJ” Shannon, the mother of Kardashian “momager” Kris Jenner, has died, Jenner announced on July 16. Read what she read
story: Mary Jo “MJ” Shannon, the mother of Kardashian “momager” Kris Jenner, has died, Jenner announced on July 16. She was 91 years old.
Jenner shared a heartfelt post about her mother, describing her as the “heart of our family.”

“Today, we said goodbye to my beautiful Mommy MJ,” Jenner said of Shannon in her social media post. “There are no words that could ever capture what she has meant to me or the heartbreak of having to say goodbye.”

In her social media post, Jenner reflected on the ways in which Shannon, known to fans of “The Kardashians” as “MJ,” had impacted her throughout the course her life. Shannon was the grandmother to the family’s famous stars including Kim Kardashian, Kourtney Kardashian, Kendall Jenner and Kylie Jenner.

“She taught me everything that truly matters… to love your family fiercely, to be kind, to show up for the people you love, and to never take a single moment together for granted,” Jenner wrote. “She taught us that family is everything. She showed us how to love unconditionally and how to find joy in the little moments. She showed me how to face life’s challenges with resilience and faith.”
Jenner, who said she was grateful for “every sacrifice” her mother made, also shared the aspects of Shannon that she will grieve.

“I will miss our daily talks, your smile, your laughter… Our hearts are broken, but we find comfort knowing that love like yours never truly leaves us,” Jenner wrote. “Your love will live on in our family, in our traditions, in every moment we are together, and in every life you touched.”
While Jenner said that the loss will be difficult for her and the family, she added that Shannon’s memory will live on.

“When I look at my kids and my grandkids, I will forever see pieces of you in all of us. There is not a part of me that isn’t shaped by you. And if I have done anything right in this world, it’s because I spent my life trying to live in a way that would make you proud,” Jenner wrote. “Every memory, every moment, every blessing, it was all because of you, and I will forever thank God every single day for making you my mommy.”
Jenner concluded her post by thanking Shannon for “giving us everything.”
“My heart is broken into a million pieces… thank you for giving me the greatest childhood and oh what a beautiful blessed life…” Jenner wrote. “I love you forever Mommy.”

In the past, Jenner has opened up about how Shannon’s health. During a 2025 episode of “The Kardashians,” Jenner broke down when reflecting on her mother’s well-being after Karen Houghton, Shannon’s younger daughter, died unexpectedly in 2024.
“Ever since my sister passed away, she’s been super sad, like we all have, and I know that I need to be there for her,” Jenner said.
In the episode, Shannon revealed she hadn’t been to her kitchen for two days due to pain she had been experiencing.
“This makes me really sad,” an emotional Jenner said in the episode. “I just hate it when she’s in so much pain.”

title: Keyne, Baby Brother of Spanish Soccer Star Lamine Yamal, Is Stealing the World Cup Spotlight
summary: The 3-year-old brother of Spanish phenom Lamine Yamal has captured the internet’s attention during the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
story: On the pitch, young phenom Lamine Yamal has been delighting soccer fans as he looks to secure the 2026 FIFA World Cup victory for Spain. But in the stands, it’s his adorable 3-year-old brother Keyne who has been keeping viewers entertained.

Yamal, 19, and his teammates are headed to the World Cup finals game against Argentina on July 19. Spain has overcome multiple difficult opponents, including France in their semifinal matchup. And Yamal’s younger brother could be their good luck charm.

Throughout the tournament, Keyne — Yamal’s half-brother who shares their mother Sheila Ebana — has been charming viewers with his excitement for his big brother and adorable fan interactions. Social media users just can’t get enough.

One fan shared an adorable video on X, featuring an excited Keyne, passionately shouting “vamos” when Spain defeated Austria 3-1 in the round of 32 on July 2. The video received more than 32,000 likes.
Yamal, who was named the player of the match, opened up about his relationship with his brother after the intense game.
“I’m moved when I see my little brother this happy, as well as seeing my mum and friends living the life they always dreamed of,” he said, according to The New York Times’ The Athletic.
He sweetly added: “My little brother means everything to me. I am in love with him; it feels like he is my son.”

In another viral moment, during Spain’s match against Belgium in the quarterfinals on July 10, an enthused Keyne was caught on camera, making silly faces and sticking out his tongue. Yamal appeared to laugh after catching a glimpse of his baby brother on the Jumbotron. That moment similarly got a lot of love from fans, drawing upwards of 38,000 likes in one social media post.
And another cute picture of Keyne waving to Yamal after Spain’s 2-0 win over France on July 14, shared by ESPN’s SportsCenter, went viral as well.

Following that match, Yamal shared a carousel on Instagram to celebrate. The final snap showed the soccer star, sitting with Keyne and Ebana in the stands. In the photo, Yamal is staring at his baby bro.
Throughout the tournament, Ebana has been giving fans a glimpse into the adventures that she’s been having with Keyne as they travel the U.S. amid the contest.

On July 5, she shared videos on Instagram of their day at the Santa Monica Pier and Venice Beach in Los Angeles. Ebana also posted videos days later of the family’s visit to the Hollywood Walk of Fame, where Keyne encountered a Freddy Krueger impersonator. In the clip, the brave 3-year-old appears to be more excited than scared. Because he’s a legend.
As shown in social media posts, Ebana and Keyne also hiked to LA’s iconic Hollywood Sign and visited the Griffith Observatory.

More photos of Keyne’s adventures were shared when Yamal celebrated his 19th birthday on July 13. Proud mom Ebana uploaded snaps that Keyne, holding some gold-colored “19” balloons. In another snap, Keyne stares up at Yamal, who’s looks like he’s about to blow out the candles on his two birthday cakes. One of the final photos in Ebana’s photo carousel showed the family, heading to a match while sporting Yamal’s jersey.

title: Chloe Fineman Leaving ‘SNL’ After 7 Seasons: ‘Greatest Privilege of My Life’
summary: Chloe Fineman revealed that she is leaving “Saturday Night Live” after being on the show for seven seasons.
story: After seven seasons of viral sketches and celebrity impressions, Chloe Fineman is leaving “Saturday Night Live” ahead of its 52nd season.
The comedian announced on Instagram July 16 that she is departing from the show, describing her time on the comedy staple as “the greatest privilege” of her life.

“It’s really hard to leave SNL but it does feel like the right time,” Fineman wrote. “I’m going to miss it a lot. But the people who work there are my family and that place is my home, and I know I’ll never be too far away.”

Her departure follows a slew of exits from many of the show’s veteran comedians in 2025, including Heidi Gardner, Ego Nwodim and Bowen Yang, as well as Michael Longfellow, Devon Walker and Emil Wakim, who were shorter-tenured performers.
Ahead of the Season 51 premiere in September 2025, Fineman told Extra TV that she was still wrapping her head around the shakeups.
“Some shocking stuff,” she said. “A little heartbreak, sadness. I haven’t fully processed anything, but I will say the show has such a turnover.”

In the post announcing her departure, Fineman wrote about the highs and lows of working on the show: “I still can’t really believe I got to be a part of it. I fell in love with the place the second I walked through the door.”

She also joked about the plights of working on “SNL,” recalling how performers can “sob uncontrollably” when a sketch is cut, only to look back “a few years later” and realize “it was a sketch called ‘lipstick for thicc dogs.’”
Fineman wrapped up her farewell message with a final declaration about the sketch: “And I swear to God, one day, sometime in the future, they WILL make lipstick for thicc dogs,” she wrote.

title: Jenna Bush Hager Reacts to Will Ferrell’s Impression of Her Dad: ‘I Was Hoping This Was Coming!’
summary: Jenna Bush Hager laughed when Will Ferrell did his impression of her father, former President George W. Bush, on TODAY.
story: Jenna Bush Hager still can’t get enough of Will Ferrell’s impression of her father, former President George W. Bush.

Much to her delight, the funnyman broke out his classic impression of her dad when he stopped by TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle on July 16, along with Molly Shannon, Luke Wilson, Fortune Feimster and Jimmy Tatro, his costars from Netflix’s new golf comedy “The Hawk.” The group played a game of “Putt or Dare,” where they had to perform a challenge if they missed a short putt.

Ferrell was tasked with doing three celebrity impressions after he came up just short on his shot. First, he spoke as of Ron Burgundy, his beloved character from the “Anchorman” movies. Then he resurfaced his well-known take on late baseball broadcaster Harry Caray.
He then launched into his final impression: Jenna’s father, George W. Bush, whom he often portrayed during his time on “Saturday Night Live.”
“Here’s the thing about golf ...” he began.
“I was hoping this was coming!” Jenna said.
Ferrell then looked at Jenna as he continued.
“We used to talk about this when you were just a little girl,” he said while everyone, including Jenna, laughed.
“You need a lot of strategery to get the ball in the hole,” he continued, as he fought off laughter.
“That’s your dad,” Ferrell, who turned 59 on July 16, said, finally breaking character while everyone applauded.

Ferrell made the word “strategery” famous during a 2000 “Saturday Night Live” sketch in which Ferrell’s Bush squared off against Darrell Hammond’s Al Gore in a presidential debate. Contrary to popular belief, Bush never used the word “strategery.” It was created by longtime “Saturday Night Live” writer Jim Downey.
Ferrell has busted out the impression on TODAY before.
“Here’s a funny story: I didn’t realize that I never said ‘strategery,’” he said in a Bush voice during a 2022 appearance with Hoda Kotb and Jenna. “Someone else wrote that.”
Jenna confirmed that her father never actually said the word. Despite that, she said her dad never had a problem with Ferrell — or anyone else — parodying him.

“I like to harass my dad,” Jenna said in 2024 on TODAY with Hoda & Jenna. “When he was the president, Barbara and I would show him the ‘Saturday Night Live’s’ where they made fun of him and stuff. He loved it.”
She also said her dad understood that getting lampooned came with the job.

“If you’re going to be the president of the United States, people are going to make fun of you,” she said. “And guess what, it ain’t just about you. That’s how it is, man. That’s how it’s always been.”

title: TSA Has Thoughts After Erling Haaland Seen Carrying a Taxidermy Raccoon Off a Plane
summary: Norway striker Erling Haaland was photographed holding a taxidermy raccoon holding an empty liquor bottle. TSA responded.
story: Norway’s striker Erling Haaland spent his summer in the United States playing in the World Cup, and returned home with a unique souvenir.
The 25-year-old soccer star made headlines when he was photographed carrying a taxidermy raccoon holding an empty liquor bottle when getting off a plane at Oslo’s Gardermoen Airport on July 13.
Sharing a photo from his arrival to his X account, Haaland quipped, “It followed me home.”
As the photos of him and his gift went viral, it caught the attention of the Transportation Security Administration (TSA), who shared some thoughts on what people can and can’t fly with.
“We’re getting some questions about flying with taxidermy raccoons holding empty liquor bottles,” reads TSA’s July 14 message on social media. “It’s ok with us but pls check with your airline first.”

The taxidermy raccoon was purchased during his visit to Wild Bill’s Western Store in Dallas, according to the local store. On their Instagram story, they shared Haaland’s photo and commented, “We know that raccoon! so cool seeing our little raccoon made it to Norway.”
Haaland filmed his visit to the store and shared the experience in a July 3 YouTube video he titled “Norway’s Texas Takeover.”

The 10-minute vlog shows the athlete trying on a variety of western wear, including boots and hats. It appears that he purchased “four hats, three winter hats and one summer” hat, according to the salesman in the video.
While shopping around, Haaland also expressed interest in a shirt that said, “Y’all can kiss my Dallas.”
Haaland, who became an online sensation for U.S. World Cup viewers, couldn’t believe how welcoming everyone was.
“Unbelievable, so nice. I’m coming back here,” he said. “People are so nice here. So positive. Don’t know what it is, they’re... enjoying life. It’s amazing.”
Haaland and the rest of Team Norway were unfortunately eliminated during the quarterfinals. They returned to their home country after they lost to England on July 11.
Since Haaland’s visit, sales from Wild Bill’s have skyrocketed. The store has even begun to offer international shipping for the first time in its history, owner Julie Newport told The Athletic.

“We are somewhere around 2,000 online orders right now, about 30 per cent of that is international but every day when we wake up, we have more orders,” Newport told the outlet. “For international, we just didn’t have that ability turned on before (Haaland visited).”
While Haaland didn’t share footage of his raccoon purchase, which retails for $750, the store still experienced significant interest in its taxidermy selection.

“We’ve had a couple of these taxidermy raccoons in the store for the last few years, and he obviously gravitated to that and a couple of the squirrels,” Newport told The Athletic. “(Since he posted on social media), we ordered another raccoon — we put it out on the floor today but by the time we put it on the floor, someone already bought it online.”
Unfortunately, the taxidermy specialist from whom the store purchased its critters has retired, so there is limited stock of the famous raccoon, Newport told the outlet.
The store isn’t shy about its association to Haaland. Its website proudly displays a blurb about its famous fan.

“Looking for one of the most talked-about souvenirs at Wild Bill’s?” the website says. “Our squirrels and raccoons gained worldwide attention after soccer superstar Erling Haaland shared photos from his visit to Wild Bill’s Western Store during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, introducing millions of fans to one of Texas’ most unexpected western traditions.”

title: Anne Hathaway Tears up At TODAY’s ‘Odyssey’-Themed Baby Gift: ‘Appropriately Epic’
summary: Anne Hathaway, currently pregnant with her third child, received a crochet baby outfit inspired by the “Odyssey” during her interview with Tom Holland on TODAY.
story: Homer’s epic poem warns that accepting a gift can be a dangerous decision. But “The Odyssey” star Anne Hathaway was seemingly moved to tears by TODAY’s present for her baby-on-the-way.

During an interview July 16 alongside her onscreen son Tom Holland, Craig Melvin surprised Hathaway with a custom “Odyssey”-inspired crochet baby outfit. The ensemble, resembling battle armor, included a diaper cover, a cape and a helmet.
“When the child comes out, we want the child ready for battle,” Craig joked.
Hathaway appeared particularly excited about the cape included with the outfit.
“This is appropriately epic, thank you so much,” she said.
Holland was equally impressed by the crochet handiwork.
“Tom, when you have your child,” Craig said, before Holland added, “I know where to come. I’ll come right back here.”
Hathaway, 43, announced her pregnancy with baby No. 3 via Instagram in June. She and her husband Adam Shulman, who married in 2012, are already parents to sons Jonathan, 10, and Jack, 6.
“x Baby, I’m yours x,” Hathaway captioned the clip of her showing off her baby bump for the first time, set to the tune of Barbara Lewis’ “Baby, I’m Yours.”
Prior to giving Hathaway her gift, Craig read a social media post praising the actor for balancing her packed slate of projects with her growing family.
“Anne Hathaway having 5 movies premiering this year and then announcing that she’s pregnant is the level of productivity that men can’t achieve,” the post on X read.
“I mean (men) are at a disadvantage,” Hathaway replied through laughter. “It’s just a literal truth.”
“It’s amazing,” Craig said, “You’ve made everyone else in Hollywood look and feel lazy.”
Hathaway said throughout her career she’s experienced peaks, valleys and “everything in between.”
“It’s just crazy to have a time like this where you pull these cards, and the thing that’s so exciting is they’re films that audiences want to see,” she said.

“To be a part of something, a part of year where so many people are just excited to go out, experience cinema,” she added. “And then yeah, to have this personal thing going on at the same time. It’s amazing.”
In the spring, Hathaway rolled out “Mother Mary” and “The Devil Wears Prada 2.” Now, she’s gearing up for the premieres of “The Odyssey,” “The End of Oak Street” and “Verity.”
“The Odyssey” hits theaters July 17.

title: ‘The Odyssey’ Reviews: What Critics Said to Earn the Movie a 98% Rotten Tomatoes Score
summary: Here is what the critics are saying about Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” which stars Matt Damon, Charlize Theron, Anne Hathaway and Tom Holland.
story: It looks like Christopher Nolan may have hit a Homer-run with the “The Odyssey.” The 172-minute blockbuster, written and directed by the “Oppenheimer” Academy Award winner, is poised to be one of the films of the summer, and the reviews may back up all the hype.

The long-awaited movie, starring Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Charlize Theron, Tom Holland, Zendaya, Samantha Morton, Robert Pattinson, Lupita Nyong’o, Elliot Page and Jon Bernthal hits theaters July 17.
“The Odyssey” is an adaptation of Homer’s classic poem, revolving around the Greek king Odysseus (played by Damon), who endures a long and daunting journey home after the Trojan War.
The early reaction to the film was favorable, but now the reviews are in, and it looks like the film may very well live up to the hoopla, earning a decadent 98% score on Rotten Tomatoes.
Here’s a look at what the critics are saying about “The Odyssey.”
Variety
Guy Lodge lauded the scope and ambition of the movie.

“A genuinely grand, gutsy vision, “The Odyssey” thrills generously for the bulk of its near three-hour running time: Every few minutes, it seems, it throws at its audience another mighty set piece that, in almost any other summer studio spectacle, would be a climactic standout,” he wrote in his review for Variety.
Lodge liked the “inspired casting of Matt Damon” and the other casting decisions.

“The Odyssey” is a veritable banquet, then, of such loud, grandiose, movie-movie pleasures, so brashly, confidently lavish that it can afford to throw away a significant portion of its all-star cast on lily-gilding cameos,” he wrote.

“There’s so much to feel here at a sensory level that the film gets away with its slightly aloof, soul-skirting chill; we leave it feeling that we’ve been to hell and back, and exhilaratingly so,” he added.
Rolling Stone
“Nolan and his behind-the-camera collaborators want to wow you,” wrote David Fear, who ultimately concludes that’s exactly what he does.

“What you tend to walk away with after bearing witness to ‘The Odyssey,’ arguably Christopher Nolan’s best work after 2017’s ‘Dunkirk,’ is an overall sensation of awe,” he wrote in wrapping up his review.

“It is one of the most dynamic movies in recent memory, simply in the way it attempts to — and largely succeeds — balance such incredible highs and delicate lows, deafening bursts of divine wrath with quiet pauses of contemplation, episodic moments of old-school Saturday-matinee fantasy with the sort of grounded interactions associated with smaller projects.

“A cynical wiseass might, sight unseen, crack that it took one of the greatest epic tales ever told to finally find material that matched Nolan’s ambitions. Once you’ve stepped into this film and let it sweep you up, however, it’s hard to deny the accomplishment that he’s brought to the screen. You may have no idea how long you’ve been gone after you’ve seen it. You just know that you want to go back again.”
The Hollywood Reporter
For The Hollywood Reporter, David Rooney did call the movie “uneven,” but singled out many of the film’s performances.

“Damon is superb, going to dark places seldom if ever explored in his previous roles; Hathaway is a model of steely self-possession masking vulnerability; Pattinson bites into his character’s villainy with gusto, showing Antinous to be a cowardly conspirator, loyal only to himself,” he wrote.
He also lauded the action sequences.
“The push for in-camera spectacle over digital fakery wherever possible pays off in terms of dropping the audience right into the middle of the action,” he wrote.
Associated Press
Jake Coyle wrote for the Associated Press that Damon took on “the role of his life” in this “richly textured film.”
“While ‘The Odyssey,’ Nolan’s first film shot entirely with IMAX cameras, doesn’t skimp on grandiosity, it works surprisingly well as a simpler, human-sized tale,” he wrote.
Coyle also said the movie will take its place in the Nolan canon.

“But ‘The Odyssey’ is rarely not transfixing, and it’s a ripping adventure story, besides. At the least, it’s the definitive big-screen adaptation of one of literature’s oldest tales — a not-too-shabby accomplishment for a filmmaker of restless ambition,” he wrote.
Forbes
“‘The Odyssey’ is a visual masterpiece filled with grand production and set designs, detailed costumes, and the most unsettling action sequences,” Laura Sirikul wrote.

“The war and fight sequences, particularly in the final act, are a masterclass in storytelling, direction, sound, music, set design and action. All of which feels grand in scale and heart-pounding, as if we were there,” she continued.
She wrapped up her take on the film by praising it as a classic.
“It’s a tale that only Nolan could have really told with this massive Hollywood production — and he did it epically,” she wrote.
The New York Times
Manohla Dargis was in awe of Nolan’s work, pointing out how it effortlessly slides into his catalog of pictures.

“Nolan’s love of movies and commitment to them — to what they can do, what they can be, what they should be — runs like an electric current through his filmography, lighting it, and oftentimes you, up,” she wrote.

“That passion is in every frame of his monumental adaptation of ‘The Odyssey,’ one of the most Nolan of Nolan spectacles in its thematic concerns, formal playfulness, kinetic thrills and unabashed showmanship.”
“Nolan’s gifts are excessively obvious, and even when his characters don’t stir you, his filmmaking does,” she continued.

“Among other qualities, he doesn’t know how to make an ugly image and this one is filled with rapturous beauty. Nolan employs beauty strategically, using it to seduce viewers into stories that can seem needlessly byzantine to some — especially by impoverished mainstream industry standards — more the provenance of the art house than the multiplex. Nolan asks us to dream bigger. His ‘Odyssey’ is a classic in every sense, a transporting affirmation of the art and a work of pure cinema.”
Mashable
Belen Edwards bowed down at the foot of Nolan’s work, citing his efforts into a new genre.
“So, how does Nolan approach his first foray into epic fantasy? How does he fare when turning his lens to antiquity and one of its foundational myths?” Edwards wrote.

“The answer, in a word, is spectacularly. Nolan eschews the sleek modernity that’s come to define his filmography. Instead, he gives himself up to a grimy, haunting take on ‘The Odyssey’ that weaves myth and history into a devastating, unforgettable reckoning for Odysseus himself.”
Edwards also saluted Nolan’s ability to work on a grand scale, while also maintaining a personal touch.

“‘The Odyssey’s’ magnificent conclusion would not work if Nolan didn’t hold audiences close to the action every step of the way. Yes, the film is a glorious spectacle, boasting vast ocean vistas, armies of giants, and even the occasional sea monster. But Nolan doesn’t just want ‘The Odyssey’ to be epic. He wants it to be human, too.”
NME

“The word ‘epic’ has been tossed around a lot over the last 3,000 years… Leave it to Christopher Nolan, then, to remind us what a proper epic looks, sounds and feels like,” Paul Bradshaw began his five-star review. If ‘Oppenheimer’ was a small story made big, ‘The Odyssey’ is a big story made impossibly huge: delivering yet another landmark summer cinema event that might just be the director’s most accomplished film to date.”
Bradshaw also marveled at Nolan’s ability to make sense of a complex story.
“Always a master of structure, Nolan’s real coup here is cutting the poem up into bits and piecing it all back together again,” he wrote.

“Less a case of them not making ‘em like they used to, watching the film leaves you with a sense that this sort of thing probably won’t be made at all for too much longer — the sheer scale, ambition and weight of it seeming to belong to a different world already,” he added. “It’s hard to see how cinema can get much bigger than this.”

title: Jennifer Garner Hosted Her Own ‘Five-Star Weekend’: ‘I Kind of Threw Myself a Wedding’
summary: Jen Garner and Elin Hilderbrand joined Jenna Bush Hager on her podcast Open Book With Jenna on an episode that aired on July 16.
story: In Elin Hilderbrand’s bestselling novel “The Five-Star Weekend,” food influencer Hollis Shaw, reeling from the sudden death of her husband, invites four friends from four different stages of life to a weekend away in Nantucket, Massachusetts.
What begins as a heartfelt attempt to reconnect quickly unravels as long-buried secrets come to the surface, old wounds are reopened and the women confront major life decisions.
Jennifer Garner, who stars as Hollis in Peacock’s adaptation of the novel, said she’s experienced her own version of a “Five-Star Weekend” in real life.

Speaking with Jenna on the July 16 episode of her “Open Book with Jenna” podcast, where Hilderbrand also appeared as a guest, Garner reflected on her latest “Five-Star”-adjacent extravaganza: Gathering friends from every chapter of her life for her 50th birthday on April 17, 2022.
“I just had friends from my whole life. I kind of threw myself a wedding,” said Garner, now 54.

The milestone birthday happened to fall on Easter for the first time in her life, she said, granting her an extra-long celebration. More importantly, it gave the actor an opportunity to bring people together who rarely crossed over.

“One night it was just the girls, and it was so special and fun because I also have this little posse of works friends that I shoot with, like the people I’ve been with forever since ‘Alias,’ and they were part of it as well,” she explained.
“Usually it’s like when I’m with when I’m working, I live that life, and otherwise I just see them now and then. So to have everybody together was especially special.”

The jam-packed weekend also featured a memorable surprise from Garner’s teen crush, Donny Osmond, TODAY.com previously reported. The singer appeared with a custom cake that read: “13 going on 50! Love Donny!”
Hilderbrand, on the other hand, told Jenna that she has never quite embraced the premise of her own novel.

“For the last 33 years, (Nantucket) has been my world. So almost all of my friends are friends that I’ve met on Nantucket,” the author said. “I have my girlfriends from college and I have friends from high school, but the two worlds have not collapsed.”
“You’ve got to make it happen,” Jenna insisted.
“It would be so weird,” Hilderbrand replied, in part. “Like, would it work?”
Garner chimed in: “Yes, it would work. It’s worked for me. It’ll work for you. Women, we look for ways to connect.”

title: Savannah Guthrie Shares She’s Off to Film Wordle Game Show for a Couple of Weeks
summary: Savannah Guthrie shared on TODAY Thursday that she will be away from the show for a few weeks to film a new Wordle game show she is hosting.
story: Savannah Guthrie shared on TODAY Thursday that she will be away from the show for a few weeks to film a new Wordle game show she is hosting.
“I’m headed over to shoot ‘Wordle’ over the next few weeks,” Savnnah said on TODAY July 16. “We’re going to shoot the whole season, and we’re super excited. Cannot wait for everyone to see it.”

Savannah had previously announced on TODAY in May that she would be hosting the new NBC show, which is based on the popular online puzzle game in which you try to guess a five-letter word in six tries or less.
“The Tonight Show” host Jimmy Fallon is executive producing the new show alongside The New York Times, which owns Wordle.

“We were looking, we’re like, ‘Who’s the perfect host for this? We need to have someone that looks like they play Wordle, someone that knows how to run a show and host it.’ And we did the pilot, and you are amazing,” Fallon said about Savannah on TODAY in May.

Teams of three avid Wordle players will go head-to-head in solving puzzles on the show for a cash prize. Fallon said the show has been in development for two-plus years. Wordle made its debut in 2021 and became a pandemic obsession for millions of players. The New York Times purchased the game in 2022 and offers Wordle for free in the New York Times Games app on iOS and Android, as well as mobile web and desktop.
The game show is expected to premiere in 2027 and will air in primetime.

TODAY and The New York Times also announced in an exclusive on July 16 that fans can solve TODAY-themed Wordle puzzles for a chance to win VIP access to Citi Concert Series performances this summer by artists like Tyla, Shaboozey, Bebe Rexha and more.

title: Caitlin Clark Wishes Boyfriend Connor McCaffrey Happy Birthday With Sweet Photo
summary: Despite being among the WNBA’s most-watched players, Caitlin Clark tends to keep her personal life mostly private — including her long-term relationship with boyfriend Connor McCaffrey.
story: Despite being among the WNBA’s most-watched players, Caitlin Clark tends to keep her personal life mostly private — including her long-term relationship with boyfriend Connor McCaffrey.

For birthdays, though, the couple often shares their love more publicly. To celebrate McCaffrey’s 28th on July 13, Clark gave her fans a rare glimpse into their relationship with an affectionate Instagram post.
“Happyyyyy Birthdayyyy Con,” she captioned the post, adding heart emoji. “I love celebrating you always and can’t wait to see what this year brings you , ilyyy.”

Among the black-and-white carousel, Clark shared three photos of the couple smiling and hugging side by side. In the fourth and final shot, she captured McCaffrey cheering her on from the stands while she plays for the Indiana Fever.
“Pic 4 is us,” McCaffrey commented, acknowledging his typical role as her supporter.
“Love you thank u sm,” he commented separately, adding a black heart.
Just a few months earlier in April, Clark also gave her 3.8 million followers a glimpse at the couple’s third anniversary celebrations.
“Three years with my fav,” she captioned a photo of the smiling and dolled up couple, adding, “you’re the bestttt.”
The two met in 2023 while both playing as college athletes at the University of Iowa, where Clark famously set the NCAA Division I women’s basketball scoring record.
During his college career, McCaffrey was a standout player in his own right, finishing with the second-best career assist-to-turnover ratio in NCAA history.

While Clark went on toq keep playing professionally after the couple graduated from Iowa in 2023 — earning the 2024 WNBA Rookie of the Year award for her first season with the Fever — McCaffrey pivoted to coaching.

He spent around two years on the Butler University staff as an assistant coach for its men’s basketball team and later moved to his current position: player development assistant for the Noblesville Boom, the NBA G League affiliate of the Indiana Pacers.

title: Jon Bernthal, Who Met Tom Holland at 17, Is ‘So Proud’ Of Him: ‘He’s Still a Family-First Guy, He’s in Love’
summary: Jon Bernthal acts alongside Tom Holland in both “The Odyssey” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” this year. He recalls their friendship on TODAY.
story: There was an additional perk for Jon Bernthal when he landed roles in two of this summer’s most anticipated blockbuster movies.

Playing King Menelaus of Sparta in “The Odyssey” and reprising his role as Punisher in “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” also meant working alongside longtime friend Tom Holland. The British star plays Telemachus in “The Odyssey” and steps back into his Spidey suit for the Marvel sequel.
Asked about returning to The Punisher role a decade after he first suited up as the vigilante, Bernthal had a very specific highlight.
“Mostly for me it was two back-to-back movies that I got to do with my friend Tom Holland,” Bernthal said on TODAY July 15.
“I’ve known him since he was 17. He’s as good a man as he is an actor,” he continued. “I’m just so in awe of him and proud of him, and I love seeing the man that he’s become.”

Bernthal, 49, and Holland, 30, first appeared onscreen together in the 2017 Irish medieval film “Pilgrimage.” A year earlier, Holland made his first appearance as Spider-Man in “Captain America: Civil War,” while 2016 also marked Bernthal’s first appearance as The Punisher in “Daredevil,” before leading his own spinoff show as the character.

“We did our audition tapes together for ‘The Punisher’ and ‘Spider-Man’ when we were in Ireland when he was 17,” Bernthal said. “So to now walk on to this set and see all that he’s accomplished. And he still leads with grace, he’s still a family-first guy. He’s in love. It just was a real treat for me.”
Holland has been in a relationship with Zendaya, his co-star in “The Odyssey” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” since at least 2021, though they were rumored to be romantically linked much earlier.
After Zendaya was spotted on the red carpet with a diamond ring, the couple reportedly wed earlier this year, which Holland seemingly confirmed in a June interview with Esquire.
Asked if he had to message family members amid viral AI-generated images purporting to be from his wedding, Holland said, “No, because they were all there.”
The first of the two blockbusters featuring Bernthal, Holland and Zendaya that will be released is “The Odyssey,” which hits theaters on July 17.

The newest film from Oscar-winning director Christopher Nolan was shot entirely in IMAX across six different countries. The latest interpretation of the ancient Greek epic by the poet Homer has already been earning rave reviews from critics.
Bernthal recalled his reaction when he learned he was being cast in the film.

“You jump,” he said. “I think at the end of the day, it’s a filmmaker-driven business. (Nolan) is one of one. He’s singular. He’s doing the very thing he was put on the Earth to do, and when someone like that calls, it’s a thrill. There’s nothing I wouldn’t do for him.

“Sometimes you meet your heroes and they go so far beyond what you could ever imagine,” he added. “His work ethic, his skill, his talent, and his love, his real love for the game, is just unparalleled, and I’m so grateful that I got the chance to work with him.”
Nolan is the latest director to take on the classic tale of the ancient Greek king Odysseus and his long and arduous quest to return home after the Trojan War.
“I think it’s so enormously human,” Bernthal said. “Obviously it’s done more than stood the test of time.”

title: Halle Berry Says 1 Lesson From Her Fifth-Grade Teacher Changed Every Relationship in Her Life
summary: In an episode of Making Space, Halle Berry shares with Hoda Kotb the relationship advice she received from her 5th grade teacher that transformed her relationships.
story: Halle Berry’s love life has always been under a microscope — so much so that the 59-year-old has said she stopped doing interviews entirely for nearly a decade because she was tired of answering the same questions about her relationships.

Currently engaged to musician Van Hunt, Berry took a four-year break from dating before they met. A break she credits with getting herself to a place where she could attract the right kind of partner.

After three failed marriages, she realized that she was attracting men who were a “mirror of herself,” Halle Berry told The Cut. “People who were broken, people with childhood wounds that weren’t addressed.”
So she took a step away from dating and committed to working on herself through therapy.

“When you talk about working through things like that, how did you — or how do you — find that place? What does the work mean?” Hoda Kotb asks Berry in the July 15 episode of the Making Space Podcast. The actress and menopause advocate sat down with Kotb to talk the confidence that comes with aging, feeling better than ever as she enters her 60’s, and her new product launch with Joylux, “Juicy Like a Peach.”

“It’s for me. It’s been working on myself. You know, any time a relationship, whether it’s a personal relationship, a work relationship, even our relationships with our children and our family, it’s always two people,” says Berry. “And I learned very early on from my fifth grade teacher, Yvonne Sims — who’s my kid’s godmother —  she was the first person to tell me at 10 years old, when things were going wrong, she would always force me to take a look at my part in it.”

Berry says that Sims taught her, “This isn’t happening to you. It’s happening for you, and you’ve been a part of causing this. If this is a hot mess, you’re half the reason it’s a hot mess, right? So let’s look at the part you’re playing, so that you can have a different outcome next time. If not, you’ll keep replaying.”
The advice inspires Kotb to reflect back on her own dating history.

“Somebody once asked me if you lined up all the people who you were in deep relationships with, what would be the single thing that they would all have in common that they would say was the reason it ended?” Kotb says. “At the end of it, as I was thinking through it, mine was that I didn’t need them enough. Like I was fine. I have it. Thank you. I was never somebody who went past that area of deep emotional trust. It’s exactly what you said. It’s that link that you’re like, ‘Wait, what did I contribute? What was my thing here?’”

Berry says she’s asked this simple question about all the relationships in her life. “In every situation, I’ve always been able to look at the part I’ve played,” she says. “And while some have failed or not gone the way I had hoped, I can distill the part I played, and hopefully next time, I might make a different set of mistakes, but I’m not going to make the same exact mistake again.”
That process has allowed her to learn valuable lessons from each failed relationship.

“That’s sort of how my life has played out. I’ve made a series of mistakes, but I’ve learned from all of them because I’ve identified the part I played. And then finally get to, ‘Oh, I can start doing things differently now because I’m owning what I did to contribute to the demise.’”
“That’s some good advice from your fifth-grade teacher,” Kotb reflects, adding that the fact that she is the godparent of Berry’s children is “the best thing I’ve heard all day.”

“I’m so glad to have her in my life, and she was that teacher, which is why I’m so bowed down to teachers,” says Berry. “I think teachers make this world go round. But having one teacher that cares can make a difference in a life, and my fifth-grade teacher, I was at a crossroads — a real crossroads — and she saw that, and she just plucked me out. She’s one of my heroes.”
Kotb asks how her teacher reacted to her winning an Oscar. “Oh, she was there,” Berry says. “She was very proud and stunned like the rest of us.”

title: Is ‘The Odyssey’ Appropriate for Kids? Here’s How Scary It Is and Why It’s Rated R
summary: How violent is The Odyssey? Can kids see the Odyssey? Here’s what to know about the contents of The Odyssey.
story: 🚨 Warning: This story contains spoilers for Christopher Nolan’s movie “The Odyssey.”
Homer’s epic poem “The Odyssey” may be a staple in some school curriculums, but Christopher Nolan’s movie adaptation is less kid friendly.

The film, out July 17, received an R rating by the Motion Picture Association for violence and some language, per IMDb. The movie’s rating means theatergoers under 17 have to be accompanied by an adult to see “The Odyssey.”
Here’s what to know about the film’s contents if you’re considering bringing a younger person to see “The Odyssey.”
OK, Tell Me: How Violent Is ‘The Odyssey’?
It’s worth remembering that “The Odyssey” is a war story. Odysseus’ experiences at the Trojan War are depicted in detail, and so are the perils of his 10-year journey home.

There’s man-on-man violence and monster-on-man violence. Think: Cyclops, giants and a terrifying sea creature called Scylla — and those are only a few of the perils Odysseus and his men encounter. Let’s just say that by the end of the movie, you will have heard bones crunch.
Plus, there’s an unforgettable sequence that involves a transformation from man into pig and back again.

Celsiana Warwick, an assistant professor in the University of Iowa’s classics department who has written about “The Odyssey,” hasn’t seen the film, but isn’t surprised to hear it’s violent — the poem is, too.
“It’s kind of gory,” she tells TODAY.com of “The Odyssey.”
“There is some fairly brutal eating of people, like when the Cyclops is eating Odysseus’ crew. Then when Odysseus kills the suitors, that is also quite violent,” she continues.
In Nolan’s movie, the violence is integral to Odysseus’ journey: He’s still working through the emotional aftereffects of the Trojan War and inner conflict over his in the Greeks’ victory.
What Christopher Nolan Said About Violence in ‘The Odyssey’
Nolan, in an interview with TikTok movie commentator Juju Green, spoke about creating violence that was both realistic but not alienating to audiences.

“When violence is portrayed in an overly graphic or I suppose I’d say gratuitous way, which is a completely valid creative choice, I find myself looking away from the screen sometimes. In my films I want to try to keep people engaged. I want them to not be able to take their eyes off the screen. In that way you want to portray the violence with enough gravity that it feels real,” Nolan said.

“In the case of ‘The Odyssey,’ you’re dealing with weapons, swords and arrows, and there’s a bit of blood that goes along with that, but you’re trying to keep people locked in. You don’t want to repulse people because you want to keep their attention,” he continued.

title: ‘Love Island’s’ Bryce and Trinity Address Age Gap and Falling in Love In First Post-Villa Interview
summary: “Love Island USA” Season 8 winners Trinity Tatum and Bryce Alakai appeared on TODAY and discussed their age gap, falling in love and experiencing separation anxiety.
story: “Love Island USA” Season 8 winners Trinity Tatum and Bryce Alakai started the season as singles looking for love and left the villa as boyfriend and girlfriend, sealing their romance with their first “I love you,” said on national television.

The happy couple joined TODAY on July 15 for their first TV interview since leaving the luxurious Fiji villa. The two were crowned Season 8’s winners during the July 12 finale and were awarded a $100,000 prize to share as a couple.
Bryce told TODAY’s Craig Melvin that the reality of the show is intense emotions, anxiety and pressure.
“One thing that brings us closer is that comfort in those moments. We look at each other, like in those challenges and all of these things, I can confide in her and feel safe,” he said.
“Bringing that in the world, it’s almost like, life is the challenge,” he added.

During “Love Island USA,” the two spent six weeks isolated alongside dozens of other contestants. Bryce and Trinity coupled up on Day 1 of the show. While each considered “exploring” other potential relationships in the villa, Trinity said Bryce’s personality made her “want to work this out instead of try other people.”
In the first few episodes of the season, the biggest hurdle facing the couple was their age gap. Trinity is 22, while Bryce turned 30 while filming Season 8.
Bryce said he found Trinity to be “the most mature person on the show.”

“I felt so comfortable with her, and our laughter, she understood, like, her level of comedy and everything just showed she was just so intelligent and so beyond her age, that the age gap ended up just like completely disappearing in my mind,” he said.
Trinity added that now, “I honestly forget.”

“I honestly see it as a positive thing, because he can be very funny, he can be like — I don’t want to say childish,” she said with a laugh, “... but when it’s time to be serious and have those conversations, he knows exactly what to say. He gives the best advice.”
Craig noted that most couples don’t reach the “I love you” stage after just six weeks. But for Trinity, the pace of their relationship made perfect sense.

“We’ve been around each other for what, six weeks. We’re around each other all day, 24 hours, we’re having intimate conversations that sometimes you don’t see,” she said. “Genuinely, I feel like if you could be around somebody that long and you think you won’t fall in love? ... That’s kind of insane.

“We’re so alike that it’s like, we’re always in sync,” she added. “So genuinely, just being around him and getting to know him and the little sweet gestures and the things that he does, it definitely made me fall for him hard.”
Now after leaving Fiji, Trinity said they are currently experiencing “a little separation anxiety” whenever they’re apart.

“Something we weren’t anticipating was just like how much our connection has affected us outside of here, too,” Bryce added. “Anytime she’s like, ‘I’m gonna go run this errand,’ I’m like ‘Where’s she going?’ Like my heart rate starts, I’m like ‘What’s going on right now?’”
As for what’s next for the couple?

“We were just in Fiji like less 20 hours ago,” Bryce said. “So coming back in ... 50 days without our phones, without any access to the outside world, it’s been unreal to see everyone’s responses. It’s a little overwhelming, to be honest.”
Trinity said she doesn’t expect to spend much time in her home state of Virginia. Instead, she’s looking forward to “explore L.A. more” alongside Bryce, who calls the city home.
“I definitely want to be wherever Bryce is, that’s for sure,” she said. “I don’t like being away from him.”

title: KATSEYE Is Ready for a ‘New Era, New Aura’ In First Look at ‘Wild Hearts’ Documentary
summary: TODAY has the first look at Katseye’s first-ever cinema event, “Wild Hearts.” The film is a BTS look at recent highs and lows on their path to superstardom.
story: Get ready to see KATSEYE up close and personal on the big screen.

In a TODAY exclusive that aired on July 15, the girl group — who is part of our Citi Concert Series lineup this summer — is giving an exclusive first look at their new documentary film, “KATSEYE: Wild Hearts,” as tickets to see it in movie theaters go on sale.

Described as a love letter to the group’s fans, known as Eyekons, “KATSEYE: Wild Hearts” is a film that shows the group’s highs and lows as they enter their new era and prepare for the release of their third EP, “Wild.”

In the first “Wild Hearts” trailer, KATSEYE members Daniela Avanzini, Lara Raj, Megan Skiendiel, Sophia Laforteza and Yoonchae reflect on the last two years of their lives and how quickly they rose to fame.
The sneak peek then shows the group in intense rehearsals, performing for their devoted fans, in the recording studio and documenting their close bond.

With hits like “Pinky Up,” “Gabriela” and “Gnarly,” it’s been a whirlwind year for the group. Formed in 2023 as part of the competition series “The Debut: Dream Academy,” their experience was documented in the 2024 Netflix documentary “Pop Star Academy: KATSEYE.”
As fans got to see the setbacks and sacrifices the singers went through, they also saw them earning acclaim and being embraced by global audiences.
They’ve since been nominated for two Grammys, debuted in the top five of the Billboard 200 with their “Beautiful Chaos” EP, saw original member Manon Bannerman begin a hiatus and more.
But now, as Yoonchae quips in the trailer, KATSEYE is experiencing a “new era, new aura.”

Fans can dive into the singers’ world when “KATSEYE: Wild Hearts” arrives in theaters for a limited time on Aug. 12. Tickets are now on sale. Fans can visit KATSEYEWildHeartsFilm.com for more information.
The group’s first-ever cinema event comes two days before their EP “Wild” is released. They are also embarking on their “KATSEYE: The Wildworld Tour” in September.

title: Which ‘Legally Blonde’ Character You Are, Based on Your Zodiac Sign
summary: July 13, 2026 is the 25th anniversary of Legally Blonde. Here’s what to know about all the characters and their zodiac signs.
story: "Legally Blond" is nearing its Saturn return! The movie turned 25 on July 13, 2026, and its pop culture legacy is as strong as ever.
The prequel series “Elle,” which premiered earlier this year, follows the world’s most famous Gemini back when she was in high school.
“Legally Blonde” and “Elle” are showing, after all this time, that nothing should stop you from going after your dreams ... and wearing pink as you do.
For fun, here’s a look at who you are based on your zodiac sign.
Aries: Vivian Kensington

Vivian (Selma Blair) has a competitive side that comes out in and out of the classroom. Her combative nature aligns her with the fire sign Aries. Like the ram, who initially wants to win at all costs, but later realizes that they should suss out matters before acting impulsively on their emotions.
Taurus: Kyle O’Boyle

Kyle (Bruce Thomas) is the UPS guy who flirts with Paulette at the beauty salon in town. His rizz and charm align Kyle with the zodiac sign Taurus. Even though the bend and snap backfired and Paulette hit him in the nose, Kyle’s fixed energy keeps the good vibes and romance intact.
Gemini: Elle Woods

Elle (Reese Witherspoon) is a self-described “Gemini vegetarian,” like her dog, Brewster. Her fast-talking abilities, intellect, directness, and desire to have fun make her the ultimate Gemini. There is more depth to her than people assume. All of these reasons are insight into why Elle aligns with the air sign.
Cancer: Warner Huntington III

Warner (Matthew Davis) adheres to what his family thinks is best, making him a Cancer since they are close with their brood. Warner is also a player, and Cancer men do have a rep on TikTok for moving to and from different relationships on a whim.
Leo: Mrs. Windham-Vandermark

When Mrs. Windham-Vandermark (Raquel Welch) enters the courtroom, she exudes big Leo energy. Maybe it is her flair for over-the-top fashion or her act while testifying on the stand, but the one sure giveaway is her loyalty to Chutney (her daughter) and the diva-like vibe she puts out there in the film.
Virgo: David

David has a lot of knowledge as well as a wealth of statistics and facts about the law and other areas (due to his diverse background), which connects him to book-smart Virgo. His respectable, chill and kind demeanor is in sync with how the earth sign handles situations and friendships.
Libra: Emmett Richmond

Emmett (Luke Wilson) is sympathetic to Elle when she’s kicked out of class, proving that he has a sweet and gentle demeanor, like most Libras. His willingness to listen to her issues demonstrates that he is a true air sign with a heart of gold, making those who bear the scales proud.
Scorpio: Brooke Taylor-Windham

Scorpios are secretive, similarly to how Brooke (Ali Larter) handles her alibi. Rather than have her business be known, she’d rather be charged with a crime and sentenced to prison (relatable content for Scorpio). Clandestine behavior is a flex since they’re highly guarded and don’t want their personal life shared with everyone.
Sagittarius: Professor Elspeth Stromwell

Professor Stormwell (Holland Taylor) is tough, but genuinely cares about the law and students. She inspires Elle when she needs it, saying, “If you’re going to let one stupid prick ruin your life ... you’re not the girl I thought you were.” The archer is the motivator and teacher, like Stromwell.
Capricorn: Professor Aaron Callahan

Professor Callahan (Victor Garber) prioritizes his work and takes a calculated approach to gaining the respect of his pupils by urging them to fight for an internship. Capricorns demand excellence in their careers and those they take under their wing, like Callahan (even though he turns out to be a not-so-nice person).
Aquarius: Paulette Bonafonté

Paulette (Jennifer Coolidge) is a ride-or-die pal and a fantastic nail technician. Her quirky sense of humor aligns with the water bearer’s unique communication style and essence. Tried and true, she is always there for Elle, which is how Aquarians usually are with their best buds (they are the sign of friendship).
Pisces: Chutney Windham

Chutney (Linda Cardellini) is one of the movie’s antagonists who killed her father by accident. Her emotional declaration in court resembles the sentiments of Pisces, a water sign who gets deep into their feels. She may be a perjurer and guilty, but it’s a crime of the heart, which is how Pisces would act out.

title: Jason Kelce Says His Daughters Were ‘Incredible’ as Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s Flower Girls
summary: Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce’s four daughters played a special role in their uncle Travis Kelce’s wedding to Taylor Swift.
story: Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce’s daughters played a big role in their NFL star uncle Travis Kelce’s wedding to Taylor Swift.

The couple’s four little girls — Wyatt, 6, Elliotte, 5, Bennett, 3, and Finnley, 1 — served as flower girls when the Kansas City Chiefs tight end tied the knot with the pop star during a star-studded wedding at New York City’s Madison Square Garden on July 3.

“It was a special event for our entire family, and obviously my daughters are incredible,” Jason Kelce, 38, told the Reno Gazette Journal while he was competing in the American Century Championship celebrity golf tournament at the Edgewood Tahoe Resort in Nevada on July 11.
“They’re beautiful, they’re incredible personalities,” the proud dad added of his daughters. “And Travis and Taylor love them.”
The retired Philadelphia Eagle served as his younger brother’s best man during the ceremony.
Swift’s younger brother Austin Swift served as her “Man of Honor.”
“So, very happy we were able to be a part of it,” Jason Kelce said of the couple’s nuptials. “And more importantly, very happy for those two. It was an amazing day.”
Sports commentator Rich Eisen previously confirmed to “Entertainment Tonight” that Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce’s daughters were flower girls during the ceremony.

“The Kelce family is just awesome. You know, Kylie as well. Those four little girls who were sprinkling flower petals all over the place. It’s pretty cool, dude. It’s pretty cool,” said Eisen, who previously described the wedding as a “storybook” event.
Jason Kelce isn’t the only member of the Kelce family to break their silence about the couple’s lavish wedding ceremony.
The Kelce brothers’ mom, Donna Kelce, gave the event two thumbs up when she was asked about it at the Macy’s fireworks show on July 4.
The NFL star mom said in a video, “I really can’t say a heck of a lot, except it was magical, man.”

title: How Much of ‘The Five-Star Weekend’ Was Actually Filmed on Nantucket?
summary: Where was Five-Star Weekend filmed? INside the real locations on Nantucket island and what was actually filmed in Los Angeles.
story: In Peacock’s new hit series “The Five-Star Weekend,” its scenic Nantucket setting is so prominent, it’s practically an unofficial lead character.

Based on Elin Hilderbrand’s 2023 novel of the same name, “The Five-Star Weekend” tells the story of food influencer Hollis Shaw, played by Jennifer Garner, who grieves the sudden death of her physician husband.

Hollis invites close women friends from every stage of her life — played by Regina Hall, Chloë Sevigny, D’Arcy Carden and Gemma Chan — to join her for a girls getaway at her gorgeous Nantucket beach home.
The series depicts how locals on the Massachusetts island spend time on its sandy beaches and at its charming waterfront shops.
Viewers also get to enter inside some of Nantucket’s most beloved (and real) spots, including Bartlett’s Ocean View Farm, CRU Oyster Bar, The Chicken Box roadhouse bar and Wicked Island Bakery.
How much of “The Five-Star Weekend” was actually shot in Nantucket?
“Most of it was shot on a soundstage in Los Angeles,” Jennifer Garner said on TODAY with Jenna & Shienelle on July 13. “All the interiors.”
But the actual island figured into the show, too, which was a priority for Hilderbrand, who moved to the island herself after falling in love with it on a trip 30 years ago.

“The most wonderful thing other than the birth of my children was having ‘Five Stars’ shot on Nantucket because it is a singular place, it is unique and you can’t really imitate it,” the author said when she and Garner stopped by TODAY with Jenna and Sheinelle on July 13.
Shooting the series in another location and pretending it was Nantucket just wouldn’t have worked, added the author, who published “The Blue Book,” a guide to Nantucket in 2025.
Still, not all the island’s residents were as thrilled as Hilderbrand was to have the series filmed there.
“I feel like some of the locals pushed back a little bit because they didn’t want the disruption and also they were afraid of it becoming too popular,” said the author.
Hilderbrand is crossing her fingers that her fellow residents who watch the series will appreciate its authenticity.
“I hope when they see this show, they realize, OK, it was important that it was shot here,” she said.
Garner recalled the series’ cast and crew soaking up “every beautiful location” while filming. On their down time, they took advantage of Nantucket’s amenities.
“The cast was sailing together. We were out at dinner and doing karaoke together ... we played, we played hard,” Garner recalled.
Hilderbrand’s popularity among her fellow residents was what opened the door for them, Garner added.

Jenna Bush Hager Was Shocked By Her ‘Five-Star Weekend’ Cameo ... and Impressed!
